parties.popularity_note: First-preference vote share in the 5 September 1998 general election (137,037 votes; 35 of 65 seats).
parties.note: Christian democratic and conservative, centre-right. The infobox gives 16 January 1926 as the foundation date; the party traces its roots to the Anti-Reform Party of the 1880s. In 2017 it ran with the Democratic Party as Forza Nazzjonali. Party colour is blue; the exact shade is an approximation.

parties.popularity_note: First-preference vote share of the Malta Labour Party in the 5 September 1998 general election (124,220 votes; 30 seats).
parties.note: Social democratic, centre to centre-left. Founded in 1921 according to English Wikipedia (re-founded in 1949); Wikidata gives 15 October 1920. Renamed from Malta Labour Party to Partit Laburista at a November 2008 general conference. Sant's start as leader (1992) is from the article's section heading; Muscat's and Abela's dates are from Wikidata.

parties.popularity_note: Vote share in the 5 September 1998 general election (3,209 votes; no seats).
parties.note: Green party. Chairpersons: Wenzu Mintoff 1989-1999, Harry Vassallo 1999-2008 (his own article says 1998-2008), Arnold Cassola 2008-2009, Michael Briguglio 2009-2013, Cassola 2013-2017, Carmel Cacopardo 2017-2020. Vassallo (chair on 1 January 2000) and Briguglio are not recorded as people because no fetched source gives their birth years. Merged with the Democratic Party into AD+PD on 17 October 2020.
parties.review_note: The chair on 1 January 2000 (Harry Vassallo) is missing from leader_history because no birth year was found for him; add him if a source gives one. Confirm whether Vassallo became chair in 1998 or 1999.

parties.note: Centre to centre-left. Founded by Marlene Farrugia after she left Labour (announced June 2016; the infobox gives 21 October 2016). Won two seats on the Forza Nazzjonali list with the Nationalist Party in 2017. Later leaders Anthony Buttigieg (2017-2018) and Timothy Alden (interim, then leader) are not recorded. Merged with Democratic Alternative into AD+PD on 17 October 2020.

Green party formed by the merger of Democratic Alternative and the Democratic Party. Its colours are yellow, green and orange; the green of its predecessor is used here. No seats in the House of Representatives in 2022 or 2026.
